note: DRAFT. Every card must be checked by a person (and the Hindi by a Hindi speaker) before testers see it. Phrases that match messages to cards live in android/engine/src/main/kotlin/com/ruko/engine/Lists.kt. Format: docs/CONTRACTS.md Section 5 (v0.4). "notify" marks cards the approver allows as the weekly notification.

name.en: Fake police / CBI "digital arrest"

they_say.en: "This is the police / CBI. Your Aadhaar is linked to money laundering. You are under digital arrest."
they_say.hi: "मैं पुलिस / सीबीआई से बोल रहा हूँ। आपका आधार मनी लॉन्ड्रिंग में जुड़ा है। आप डिजिटल अरेस्ट में हैं।"

they_ask.en: Stay on the video call, tell no one, and send money "for verification" or "bail".
they_ask.hi: वीडियो कॉल पर बने रहें, किसी को न बताएं, और "जाँच" या "ज़मानत" के लिए पैसे भेजें।

red_flag.en: There is no "digital arrest" in Indian law. Police never arrest anyone on a call or ask for money.
red_flag.hi: भारत के कानून में "डिजिटल अरेस्ट" जैसा कुछ नहीं है। पुलिस कभी फ़ोन पर गिरफ़्तार नहीं करती और पैसे नहीं माँगती।

do.en: Hang up. Call someone you trust. Report it on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
do.hi: फ़ोन काट दें। किसी भरोसेमंद व्यक्ति को फ़ोन करें। 1930 या cybercrime.gov.in पर शिकायत करें।

name.en: Fake TRAI "your SIM will be blocked" call
name.hi: नकली TRAI कॉल: "आपका सिम बंद होगा"

they_say.en: "This is TRAI. Your SIM will be blocked in 2 hours because it was misused. Press 9 to talk to an officer."
they_say.hi: "मैं TRAI से हूँ। आपका सिम ग़लत काम में इस्तेमाल हुआ है, 2 घंटे में बंद हो जाएगा। अफ़सर से बात करने के लिए 9 दबाएं।"

they_ask.en: Talk to an "officer", who then hands you to fake police asking for money.
they_ask.hi: "अफ़सर" से बात करें, जो फिर आपको नकली पुलिस से जोड़ता है जो पैसे माँगती है।

red_flag.en: TRAI does not call people to block SIMs.
red_flag.hi: TRAI किसी को सिम बंद करने के लिए फ़ोन नहीं करता।

do.en: Hang up. If worried, check your number on the government's Sanchar Saathi website. Report on 1930.
do.hi: फ़ोन काट दें। चिंता हो तो सरकार की संचार साथी वेबसाइट पर अपना नंबर जाँचें। 1930 पर शिकायत करें।

name.en: Fake courier: "drugs found in your parcel"
name.hi: नकली कूरियर: "आपके पार्सल में ड्रग्स मिले"

they_say.en: "FedEx / DHL here. A parcel in your name has drugs and fake passports. Customs has seized it."
they_say.hi: "FedEx / DHL से बोल रहे हैं। आपके नाम के पार्सल में ड्रग्स और नकली पासपोर्ट मिले हैं। कस्टम ने ज़ब्त कर लिया है।"

they_ask.en: Talk to "Mumbai police", then pay to "clear your name".
they_ask.hi: "मुंबई पुलिस" से बात करें, फिर "नाम साफ़ करने" के लिए पैसे दें।

red_flag.en: Courier companies don't connect you to the police, and police don't take money on calls.
red_flag.hi: कूरियर कंपनियाँ आपको पुलिस से नहीं जोड़तीं, और पुलिस फ़ोन पर पैसे नहीं लेती।

do.en: Hang up. Don't pay. Report on 1930.
do.hi: फ़ोन काट दें। पैसे न दें। 1930 पर शिकायत करें।

name.en: Fake bank "KYC expired" message
name.hi: नकली बैंक मैसेज: "KYC खत्म हो गई"

they_say.en: "Your bank KYC has expired. Your account will be blocked today. Update now: [link]"
they_say.hi: "आपकी बैंक KYC खत्म हो गई है। आज आपका खाता बंद हो जाएगा। अभी अपडेट करें: [लिंक]"

they_ask.en: Open a link, enter your details or OTP, or install an app.
they_ask.hi: लिंक खोलें, अपनी जानकारी या OTP डालें, या कोई ऐप इंस्टॉल करें।

red_flag.en: Real bank texts come from registered names like VM-SBIINB, not mobile numbers. Banks never ask for your OTP or PIN.
red_flag.hi: असली बैंक मैसेज VM-SBIINB जैसे रजिस्टर्ड नाम से आते हैं, मोबाइल नंबर से नहीं। बैंक कभी OTP या PIN नहीं माँगते।

do.en: Don't tap the link. Open your bank's own app yourself, or visit the branch.
do.hi: लिंक न खोलें। अपने बैंक का ऐप खुद खोलें, या ब्रांच जाएं।

name.en: Fake "your electricity will be cut tonight"
name.hi: नकली मैसेज: "आज रात बिजली कट जाएगी"

they_say.en: "Your electricity will be cut tonight at 9:30 because your bill isn't updated. Call this officer."
they_say.hi: "आपका बिल अपडेट नहीं है, आज रात 9:30 बजे बिजली कट जाएगी। इस अफ़सर को फ़ोन करें।"

they_ask.en: Install an app (often a remote-control app or an APK) to "update the bill".
they_ask.hi: "बिल अपडेट" के लिए कोई ऐप इंस्टॉल करें (अक्सर रिमोट-कंट्रोल ऐप या APK फ़ाइल)।

red_flag.en: Electricity boards don't send cut-off warnings from mobile numbers or ask you to install apps.
red_flag.hi: बिजली विभाग मोबाइल नंबर से कटौती की चेतावनी नहीं भेजता और ऐप इंस्टॉल करने को नहीं कहता।

do.en: Ignore it. Check your bill only on the electricity board's official app or website.
do.hi: इसे अनदेखा करें। अपना बिल सिर्फ़ बिजली विभाग के असली ऐप या वेबसाइट पर देखें।

name.en: Fake credit-card reward points

they_say.en: "Your credit card reward points expire today. Redeem them for cash now."
they_say.hi: "आपके क्रेडिट कार्ड के रिवॉर्ड पॉइंट आज खत्म हो जाएंगे। अभी कैश में बदलें।"

they_ask.en: Install an app or open a link and type in your card details.
they_ask.hi: कोई ऐप इंस्टॉल करें या लिंक खोलकर कार्ड की जानकारी डालें।

red_flag.en: Banks never send app files on WhatsApp. Points are redeemed only in the bank's own app.
red_flag.hi: बैंक कभी WhatsApp पर ऐप फ़ाइल नहीं भेजते। पॉइंट सिर्फ़ बैंक के अपने ऐप में मिलते हैं।

do.en: Don't install anything. Check your points in your bank's own app.
do.hi: कुछ भी इंस्टॉल न करें। अपने पॉइंट बैंक के अपने ऐप में देखें।

name.en: Fake customer-care number

they_say.en: You searched online for a helpline. The "agent" says they'll fix your refund or problem.
they_say.hi: आपने ऑनलाइन हेल्पलाइन खोजी। "एजेंट" कहता है कि वह आपका रिफ़ंड या समस्या ठीक कर देगा।

they_ask.en: Install AnyDesk or a screen-sharing app, share an OTP, or pay a small "fee".
they_ask.hi: AnyDesk या स्क्रीन-शेयर ऐप इंस्टॉल करें, OTP बताएं, या छोटी "फ़ीस" भरें।

red_flag.en: Real support never asks you to install a remote-control app or share an OTP.
red_flag.hi: असली कस्टमर केयर कभी रिमोट-कंट्रोल ऐप इंस्टॉल करने या OTP बताने को नहीं कहता।

do.en: Hang up. Use only the number printed on your card or shown inside the company's own app.
do.hi: फ़ोन काट दें। सिर्फ़ अपने कार्ड पर छपा नंबर या कंपनी के अपने ऐप में दिया नंबर इस्तेमाल करें।

name.en: Fake stock-tips group and trading app
name.hi: नकली शेयर-टिप्स ग्रुप और ट्रेडिंग ऐप

they_say.en: "Join our VIP stock group. SEBI registered. Guaranteed returns. Use our trading app."
they_say.hi: "हमारे VIP शेयर ग्रुप से जुड़ें। SEBI रजिस्टर्ड। पक्का मुनाफ़ा। हमारा ट्रेडिंग ऐप इस्तेमाल करें।"

they_ask.en: Invest through their app. When you try to withdraw, pay a "tax" or "fee" first.
they_ask.hi: उनके ऐप से पैसे लगाएं। निकालने पर पहले "टैक्स" या "फ़ीस" भरें।

red_flag.en: No one can guarantee returns. Having to pay before you can withdraw means it's a scam.
red_flag.hi: कोई भी पक्का मुनाफ़ा नहीं दे सकता। पैसे निकालने से पहले पैसे माँगना मतलब धोखा।

do.en: Invest only through a broker you already know. Check registrations on sebi.gov.in.
do.hi: सिर्फ़ उसी ब्रोकर से निवेश करें जिसे आप पहले से जानते हैं। sebi.gov.in पर रजिस्ट्रेशन जाँचें।

name.en: Fake part-time job / online tasks

they_say.en: "Earn ₹200 per review or like, from home." They pay small amounts at first.
they_say.hi: "घर बैठे हर रिव्यू या लाइक पर ₹200 कमाएं।" शुरू में छोटी रकम देते हैं।

they_ask.en: Pay for "prepaid tasks" in a Telegram group to earn more.
they_ask.hi: ज़्यादा कमाने के लिए Telegram ग्रुप में "प्रीपेड टास्क" के पैसे भरें।

red_flag.en: A real job never asks you to pay to earn.
red_flag.hi: असली नौकरी में कमाने के लिए पैसे नहीं भरने पड़ते।

do.en: Stop and don't pay anything more. Report on 1930.
do.hi: रुक जाएं और आगे कोई पैसे न भरें। 1930 पर शिकायत करें।

name.en: Fake bank KYC, challan or wedding card sent as an app (APK)

they_say.en: "Your account will be blocked tonight. Install our official update." Then a file like "SBI KYC AADHAR UPDATE" or "Your Traffic RTO Challan" marked APK. Sometimes it comes from a known contact whose WhatsApp was hacked.

they_ask.en: Open and install the file.

red_flag.en: Banks, the RTO and the government never send apps on WhatsApp. If WhatsApp shows "APK" under a file, it is an app, not a document.

do.en: Don't open or install it. Delete the chat. Call the sender on their saved number, or your bank on the number printed on your card.

name.en: Fake family member's voice
name.hi: परिवार के सदस्य की नकली आवाज़

they_say.en: A voice that sounds exactly like your child or relative: "I've had an accident, send money now, don't tell anyone."
they_say.hi: बिल्कुल आपके बच्चे या रिश्तेदार जैसी आवाज़: "मेरा एक्सीडेंट हो गया है, अभी पैसे भेजो, किसी को मत बताना।"

they_ask.en: Send money right away, often to someone else's account.
they_ask.hi: तुरंत पैसे भेजें, अक्सर किसी और के खाते में।

red_flag.en: AI can copy a voice from a few seconds of audio. Hurry plus secrecy is the sign.
red_flag.hi: AI कुछ सेकंड की आवाज़ से नकल कर सकता है। जल्दबाज़ी और राज़ रखने को कहना ही पहचान है।

do.en: Hang up and call them back on their saved number. Ask for your family word if you have one.
do.hi: फ़ोन काटकर उन्हें उनके सेव नंबर पर वापस फ़ोन करें। परिवार का कोड-शब्द हो तो पूछें।

name.en: Fake prize, loan, job or scheme that asks for a fee first

they_say.en: "You've won Rs 25 lakh." "Your loan is approved." "You're selected for the job." "Register for the government scheme."

they_ask.en: Pay a registration, processing or claim fee first.

red_flag.en: Real prizes, loans, jobs and government schemes never ask you to pay before you receive money.

do.en: Don't pay anything. Block the number. Check schemes only on .gov.in sites. Report on 1930.

name.en: Fake “money debited” alert that asks you to reply NO

they_say.en: “Rs 48,500 has been debited from your account. If this wasn’t you, reply NO to block it.”

they_ask.en: Reply YES or NO, or call their number to “block” or “reverse” the payment.

red_flag.en: Banks never ask you to reply YES or NO on WhatsApp. Real debit alerts come by SMS from the bank’s name (like JD-SBIUPI) and tell you to call the number on your card.

do.en: Don’t reply. Open your bank’s own app to check. Block the number. If money is gone, call 1930.

name.en: Fake “money credited” SMS, then “I sent it by mistake”

they_say.en: “Rs 5,000 credited to your A/c…” Then a call: “I sent you money by mistake, please send it back.”

they_ask.en: Send the “extra” money back, often more than once.

red_flag.en: The “bank” SMS comes from an ordinary mobile number. Real alerts come from the bank’s sender name, and the money never shows in your bank app.

do.en: Check your balance in your bank’s own app. Don’t send anything back. If someone did pay you by mistake, they can ask their bank to reverse it.

name.en: Fake India Post “parcel stuck, update your address”

they_say.en: “India Post: your package is at the warehouse. Delivery failed due to incomplete address. Update it within 48 hours at this link, or it will be returned.”

they_ask.en: Open a link, type your address and card details, and pay a small “redelivery fee”.

red_flag.en: India Post never sends links to update your address. The link is not indiapost.gov.in, it only looks like it.

do.en: Don’t open the link. If you are expecting a parcel, track it on indiapost.gov.in or the India Post app.

sources.name: All India Radio (PIB Fact Check, Jan 2026)

name.en: Fake traffic e-challan with a payment link or app

they_say.en: “Your challan for vehicle PB08… is Rs 500. Pay online at this link, or contact the RTO.” Sometimes an app file named “e-Challan” or “mParivahan”.

they_ask.en: Pay through a link that copies the Parivahan site, or install an app.

red_flag.en: Real challans are checked and paid only on echallan.parivahan.gov.in. A link ending in .in, .com or .xyz instead of .gov.in is fake, and a challan never comes as an app.

do.en: Don’t open it. Check your vehicle number yourself on echallan.parivahan.gov.in.

name.en: Fake income-tax refund “approved”

they_say.en: “You have been approved an income tax refund of Rs 15,490. Verify your account number, or update your bank details at this link.”

they_ask.en: Open a short link and type bank details, card number or OTP.

red_flag.en: The Income Tax Department never sends refund links. Refunds go straight to the account already in your tax return.

do.en: Don’t open the link. Check refund status only by logging in at incometax.gov.in.

name.en: Fake government “free” scheme: laptop, recharge or cash

they_say.en: “Under the PM Free Mobile Recharge / Free Laptop Scheme, everyone gets ₹239 recharge (or a laptop, or ₹46,715). Click the link and register before the last date. Share with 10 groups.”

they_ask.en: Fill in a form with Aadhaar, bank or phone details, or pay a small “registration” fee.

red_flag.en: Real schemes are announced on .gov.in sites, not in forwards with a deadline and a strange link. PIB Fact Check has called these fake many times.

do.en: Don’t click or forward it. Check any scheme on the ministry’s own website or with PIB Fact Check.

name.en: Instant loan app: fees first, then threats

they_say.en: “Pre-approved loan of ₹3 lakh, no documents.” After you install the app: “Your loan has expired. Pay today or we will message your family and contacts.”

they_ask.en: Pay a “processing fee” first, or repay far more than you borrowed, to personal UPI IDs.

red_flag.en: Real lenders take any fee out of the loan, and are listed with RBI. Apps that read your contacts and threaten to shame you are illegal.

do.en: Don’t pay fees upfront or install loan apps from links. If you are being threatened, report it at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930, and complain on RBI’s Sachet portal.

sources.name: PIB (RBI caution on unauthorised lending apps)

name.en: Online friend’s “gift parcel” stuck at customs

they_say.en: A new friend from Instagram, Facebook or a matrimony site promises gifts from abroad. Then “Customs / Skyshield Cargo”: “Your parcel has arrived. Pay ₹40,000 clearance charges to release it.”

they_ask.en: Pay customs, clearance or “anti-money-laundering” fees, again and again.

red_flag.en: Customs never asks you to pay into a personal account or UPI ID. A stranger you met online sending costly gifts is the trap.

do.en: Don’t pay anything to release a gift. Stop talking to them and report it at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.

name.en: “I sent you a code by mistake”: WhatsApp account takeover

they_say.en: “Hi, sorry, I sent a 6-digit code to you by mistake, can you send it to me? It’s urgent.” Or a call: “Dial *21* and this number to fix your network.” Then your contacts get: “I’m in trouble, please send ₹10,000, I’ll return it tomorrow.”

they_ask.en: Share the 6-digit code you just got, or dial a code. Your friends are then asked for money from your account.

red_flag.en: That code is the key to your WhatsApp. Nobody sends a code “by mistake”. A friend asking for money by text should always be called first.

do.en: Never share a code you receive. Turn on two-step verification in WhatsApp. If a friend asks for money, call them on their usual number.

name.en: Fake buyer or seller on OLX: the “Army officer”

they_say.en: “I am in the Army, posted elsewhere, so I’m selling my scooter cheap.” Or as a buyer: “I’ll pay full price, I’m sending ₹1 to test.” Then: “I sent ₹13,500 by mistake, send back the extra.”

they_ask.en: Pay “Army cargo” or delivery fees, scan a QR code, or send back an “extra” payment.

red_flag.en: Army officers don’t sell through OLX with cargo fees. You never scan a QR code or enter a PIN to receive money.

do.en: Meet in person and see the item before paying. Never scan a QR code to receive money. Check any payment in your own bank app.

sources.name: Free Press Journal (QR codes from fake Army officer)
RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: “Scan this QR / enter your PIN to receive money”

they_say.en: “I’m sending your payment. Scan this QR code and enter your UPI PIN to receive it.” Earlier versions used a UPI “collect request” that looked like money coming in.

they_ask.en: Scan a QR code or approve a request and type your UPI PIN.

red_flag.en: You never need your PIN or a QR scan to RECEIVE money. A PIN always means money is leaving your account.

do.en: If anyone asks you to scan or enter your PIN to get paid, stop. Only use your PIN when you are paying. (Since October 2025, UPI no longer allows person-to-person collect requests, but the QR version continues.)

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: Video call from a stranger, then blackmail

they_say.en: A video call from an unknown number shows an obscene video and records your face. Then: “Pay or this video goes to your family.” Later a fake “police officer” or “YouTube official” asks for more to “delete the case”.

they_ask.en: Pay to stop the video being shared, again and again.

red_flag.en: Paying never ends it. Calls like this are recorded on purpose to blackmail you.

do.en: Don’t answer video calls from unknown numbers. If it happens, don’t pay, block them, and report at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930. You are the victim, not the guilty one.

name.en: Fake “upgrade your SIM to eSIM / 5G” call

they_say.en: “I’m from Jio / Airtel. Upgrade to eSIM (or 5G) for free. You’ll get an SMS, just tell me the code or click the link.”

they_ask.en: Share the code or click the link, which moves your number to their phone. Then all your bank OTPs go to them.

red_flag.en: Your operator never needs your OTP or a link sent on WhatsApp to change your SIM. If your phone suddenly shows no network, act at once.

do.en: Hang up and never share the code. If your signal vanishes without reason, call your operator from another phone and your bank right away.

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: Fake insurance “bonus” or policy refund call

they_say.en: “I’m calling from IRDAI. ₹4 lakh bonus is pending on your old policy” or “Your policy money was transferred to someone else; pay a fee to get it back.”

they_ask.en: Pay a fee, tax or deposit to release the money, or buy a new policy to “unlock” it.

red_flag.en: IRDAI never calls people, never announces bonuses, and never sells policies. Real insurers don’t ask for fees to pay you.

do.en: Hang up. Check your policy only with your insurer’s number from the policy papers or official website.

sources.name: IRDAI public notice: spurious calls and fake offers

name.en: Fake hotel, pilgrimage or helicopter booking

they_say.en: An ad or website: “Kedarnath helicopter tickets / Somnath guest house / Char Dham package. Book now, limited seats.” Payment by UPI to a person, then no ticket and the number stops working.

they_ask.en: Pay an advance by UPI or QR code to a personal account.

red_flag.en: Helicopter and temple bookings are sold only on official sites (for Kedarnath: heliyatra.irctc.co.in). “Sponsored” search results and Facebook pages can be fake.

do.en: Book only on the official site or a trusted agent. Don’t pay advances to personal UPI IDs.

sources.name: PIB (I4C alert on fake booking sites)

name.en: Fake shopping site or Instagram seller

they_say.en: “Branded shoes / iPhone at 90% off, today only.” A site that looks like Flipkart or Amazon, or an Instagram page that takes UPI payment.

they_ask.en: Pay in advance by UPI or card. Nothing arrives, or a cheap fake does.

red_flag.en: Huge discounts on branded goods, payment only by UPI to a person, and no cash on delivery.

do.en: Buy from known apps and sites. Check the web address carefully. Prefer cash on delivery from new sellers.

name.en: “Earn commission: rent out your bank account”

they_say.en: “Earn 3–5% commission at home. Just let us use your bank account, or open a new one for us. Money comes in, you send it on.”

they_ask.en: Hand over your account, debit card, SIM or login, or pass on money you receive.

red_flag.en: This money is stolen from scam victims. Your account gets frozen and you can be arrested, even if you only got a small commission.

do.en: Never sell, rent or lend your bank account, SIM or company papers. Report the offer at cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.

name.en: Overseas job in Thailand, Cambodia or Laos that traps you

they_say.en: “Data entry / customer support job in Thailand, ₹1 lakh a month, free flight and hotel. Simple typing test.”

they_ask.en: Travel on a tourist visa through an agent. You are then forced to work in a scam centre.

red_flag.en: Real overseas jobs come with a signed contract and a work visa, through MEA-registered agents. Never a tourist visa.

do.en: Check the agent on the eMigrate portal and with the Indian embassy before you go. Warn young family members about these offers.

name.en: Call from “the bank”: card blocked, tell the OTP

they_say.en: “I’m from SBI / RBI. A suspicious ₹48,000 transaction is on your card. To block it, tell me the OTP you just got.” Or a free credit-limit increase or lifetime-free card.

they_ask.en: Read out an OTP, CVV, card number or PIN.

red_flag.en: No bank or RBI official ever asks for an OTP, PIN or CVV. Banks now call from numbers starting 1600.

do.en: Hang up. Call the number on the back of your card yourself.

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods
Business Standard (RBI warns of fraud in its name)

name.en: Fake donation appeal after a disaster

they_say.en: “Donate to PM CARES / flood relief. UPI: pmcare@sbi.” A lookalike UPI ID or a QR code for a personal account.

they_ask.en: Pay a donation to a fake UPI ID.

red_flag.en: The UPI ID is almost right but not quite (pmcare instead of pmcares). Real relief funds are listed on .gov.in sites.

do.en: Donate only through the official website of the fund, never from a forwarded UPI ID or QR code.

name.en: Fake COVID vaccine registration call

they_say.en: “I’m from the health department, registering you for the vaccine. Tell me your Aadhaar number and the OTP.”

they_ask.en: Share Aadhaar and OTP, which empties the linked bank account.

red_flag.en: Vaccine registration never needed an OTP read out to a caller.

do.en: Never share an OTP with a caller, whatever the reason.

cards.retired_note: The pandemic drive ended. Kept so its patterns still catch the same 'tell me the OTP' script if it comes back.

name.en: Money withdrawn with a copied fingerprint (AePS)

they_say.en: No message at all. Fingerprints copied from property papers or a fake “biometric update” are used at a cash point to withdraw money through Aadhaar.

they_ask.en: Nothing. Money disappears from an Aadhaar-linked account.

red_flag.en: Withdrawals you didn’t make, at a micro-ATM or bank mitra.

do.en: Lock your biometrics in the mAadhaar app or on uidai.gov.in (unlock only when you need them). Report at once on 1930.

name.en: ATM card skimming

they_say.en: No message. A hidden device on an ATM copies your card, and a camera records your PIN.

they_ask.en: Nothing. Your card is copied and used elsewhere.

red_flag.en: A loose or bulky card slot, a strange keypad cover, or someone “helping” you at the ATM.

do.en: Cover the keypad when typing your PIN. Use ATMs inside bank branches. Turn on SMS alerts and block your card at once if something looks wrong.

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: Public phone-charging points that steal data

they_say.en: No message. A free USB charging point at a station or airport can copy data or install malware.

they_ask.en: Plug your phone into a public USB port.

red_flag.en: A USB cable or port you don’t own.

do.en: Carry your own charger and plug into a power socket, not a USB port.

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: Money-doubling chain or MLM scheme

they_say.en: “Invest ₹10,000, get ₹20,000 in 30 days. Add 3 friends and earn more.” Often with early payouts to build trust.

they_ask.en: Invest money and bring in friends and relatives.

red_flag.en: Guaranteed, fast, high returns, and earnings that depend on recruiting others. Early payouts come from newer members’ money.

do.en: Don’t invest in schemes that pay for recruiting. Check an investment is registered with SEBI or RBI.

sources.name: RBI: BE(A)WARE booklet on fraud methods

name.en: “Please merge the call with my friend”

they_say.en: A stranger says they got your number from a friend and asks you to merge the call with another number. That other line is your bank’s OTP call.

they_ask.en: Merge the calls, so the scammer hears the OTP your bank reads out.

red_flag.en: Nobody genuine needs you to merge calls. An OTP call you didn’t ask for means someone is trying to pay with your account.

do.en: Never merge calls with unknown numbers. If you get an OTP you didn’t ask for, call your bank and 1930.

name.en: Fake census or voter-list officer

they_say.en: “I’m from the Census / election office. We need to verify your family details. You’ll get an OTP, please tell me.” Or a “census verification” link or app.

they_ask.en: Share Aadhaar, bank details or an OTP, pay a fee, or install a screen-sharing app.

red_flag.en: Census and election officials never ask for OTPs, PINs, bank details or money, by phone or link. Real enumerators carry ID with a QR code.

do.en: Don’t share any OTP. Check the person’s ID, and report fake calls to 1930.

name.en: Fake gas company: “connection will be cut tonight”

they_say.en: “Dear customer, your gas connection will be disconnected tonight at 9:30 pm as last month’s bill is not updated. Call this officer.” Then an app to “update the bill” or a ₹10 “verification” payment.

they_ask.en: Install an app or pay a small amount by card, which hands over your phone or card.

red_flag.en: Gas companies don’t threaten same-night disconnection by SMS or WhatsApp, and never send apps. MGL and others say they never ask for OTPs or bank details.

do.en: Don’t call the number or install anything. Check your bill in the gas company’s own app or website.

sources.name: Free Press Journal (MGL fake APK scam)

name.en: Fake EPFO: “update KYC to withdraw your PF”

they_say.en: “Your PF account is frozen. Update KYC at this link to withdraw.” Or an “EPFO agent” offering faster PF claims for a processing fee.

they_ask.en: Share UAN, Aadhaar, OTP or bank details, or pay a fee.

red_flag.en: EPFO never asks for these by call, SMS or WhatsApp and has no agents. The only site is epfindia.gov.in.

do.en: Use only the UMANG app or epfindia.gov.in. EPFO helpline: 14470.

name.en: Fake flat or PG for rent: pay to block it

they_say.en: “Lovely 2BHK, very low rent. I’m out of town, pay ₹10,000 token to block it before others take it.” Sometimes AI photos, or a “visitor pass” fee before viewing.

they_ask.en: Pay an advance, deposit or visit fee by UPI before seeing the place.

red_flag.en: The owner can’t meet, refuses a visit, and rushes you to pay. Photos look too perfect.

do.en: Never pay before seeing the flat and meeting the owner. Check ownership with the housing society.

name.en: Fake life certificate site or call for pensioners

they_say.en: “Your pension will stop. Submit your life certificate here for ₹199.” A site like jeevanpraman.online, or a caller asking for the OTP you just got.

they_ask.en: Pay a fee, fill in your details on a copy site, or read out an OTP.

red_flag.en: The only official site is jeevanpramaan.gov.in, and it is free. Nobody needs your OTP over the phone.

do.en: Give your life certificate at your bank or post office, or on jeevanpramaan.gov.in. Never share the OTP.

name.en: Scratch card by post: “You won a car from Meesho / Naaptol”

they_say.en: A letter arrives by post with a scratch card in a shopping site’s name. It shows a car or ₹15 lakh prize. The helpline then says: “Pay registration, GST and insurance first.”

they_ask.en: Pay fees and “taxes” again and again, and send ID copies.

red_flag.en: You never pay to receive a real prize. Shopping sites don’t run lucky draws by post.

do.en: Don’t call the number on the card or pay anything. Tell the family, especially older members, about these letters.

name.en: “Your nephew in Canada is in trouble, send money now”

they_say.en: A WhatsApp call from a foreign number: “Your nephew had a fight here. He will be deported unless we pay the fine today. Don’t tell his parents.” A crying “relative” comes on the line.

they_ask.en: Send money urgently to an account or UPI ID.

red_flag.en: Urgency, secrecy and a voice you can’t quite check. Scammers pick families with children studying abroad.

do.en: Hang up and call the relative or their parents on their own number. Use your family word.
